correctness.rationale: Exact knotwise signed masses yield pointwise total variation and finite sharp extremizers. Binomial-to-Poisson total-variation convergence handles the boundary; a uniform triangular-array local CLT with Chebyshev tail bounds proves the Gaussian interior. Poisson CLT gives the boundary profile at large parameter. Exact rational exponential enclosures certify the strict witness gap. Compactness and a subsequence dichotomy prove the limiting global norm and boundary-layer localization. The standalone finite checker passed after extraction; its tests do not substitute for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Richardson acceleration of Bernstein operators is classical and useful for raising smooth-function approximation order, but it loses positivity. Sharp bounded-input amplification is a natural stability invariant that the crude coefficient-sum bound 3 does not resolve. This proof quantifies the sharp asymptotic factor by a Poisson boundary variational problem, proves it strictly larger than the Gaussian interior constant, and locates all asymptotically extremal evaluation points within O(1/n) boundary layers. These are motivated structural results about extrapolation stability rather than arbitrary numerical slices.
